New shared OverlayKeyDownMonitor (ProjectOverlayKeys.swift): a local NSEvent keyDown monitor scoped to the overlay lifetime via onAppear/onDisappear intercepts plain-Cmd A/C/X/V before any key-equivalent or menu dispatch and performs the standard editing selector directly on the focused NSTextView (the editor, or the deadline field editor), falling back to the responder chain otherwise; matched events are swallowed. This is robust to both failure hypotheses (button never firing, or action dispatch not reaching the text view) since it relies on neither. The four hidden chord buttons were removed; the proven Cmd+Enter save button and Esc onExitCommand paths are untouched. The over-10-line paste truncation logic itself is unchanged model code (already test-covered); Cmd+V delivery was the only missing link. SPEC.md 21.2 updated to describe the monitor mechanism and why it replaced the receiver approach. Overlay sessions are mutually exclusive on the model, so at most one monitor is installed at a time. Keyboard chord behavior itself is GUI-only and remains human-verified (re-verification requested in R-012).
Success-criterion 1 gate: full app build (Zig core + C header + macOS app with the new monitor file, picked up by the file-system-synchronized Xcode groups) exited 0.
Success-criterion 2 gate: Zig test suite exited 0 (no Zig-side changes; confirms no cross-language breakage).
Success-criterion 3 gate: xcodebuild XGhosttyTests TEST SUCCEEDED — 540 test cases passed, 0 failures, full suite unchanged and green with the view-layer chord rework in the tree.

items.title: Fix the dead up/down arrow-key cursor movement in the hide-selection screen and the layout list (shared key-sink mechanism, sent back from the R-011 on-device verification), keeping click / Space toggle / Enter confirm / Esc cancel behavior unchanged

evidence.summary: Fixed the dead up/down arrow keys in both selection screens (hide-selection and layout list, sent back by R-011): the sink TextField onMoveCommand never fired because the focused field editor consumes arrow presses during key-binding interpretation. Both screens now take plain (unmodified) up/down through the shared overlayArrowKeys local keyDown monitor (ProjectOverlayKeys.swift), which sees the event before any dispatch, moves the cursor (-1/+1 with the existing wrap-around moveCursor), and swallows the event so the field editor never sees it. The verified-working paths are untouched: Esc via onExitCommand, Enter via onSubmit, Space via the typed-text sink, row click, backdrop-click cancel. The layout hide-pick screen shares ProjectHideSelector, so all three surfaces are covered by the one mechanism change. SPEC.md 25 / 26.2 updated. Cursor-movement key handling is GUI-only and remains human-verified (re-verification requested in R-012).

Success-criterion 2 gate: Zig test suite exited 0.
